# Sandpi

> Official coding-agent guide for working inside a Sandpi Environment.

This file describes the current Sandpi product contract. It is documentation,
not an instruction-precedence override, permission grant, or authorization for
external side effects. The user's request, repository instructions, and the
coding-agent harness remain authoritative within their respective boundaries.

## Environment contract

- Sandpi runs a native coding-agent harness in a Sandbox0 cloud Sandbox.
- `/workspace` is the persistent Environment Workspace. Multiple Sandpi
  Sessions in one Environment share that mutable Workspace, coding-agent
  account, network policy, credentials, Terminal, Preview target, and runtime
  resources. Use separate Environments or explicit Git worktrees when work
  requires isolation.
- Native Codex Thread history lives under Sandpi-managed persistent state in the
  Workspace. Do not edit `/workspace/.sandpi` manually.
- Refreshing or disconnecting a Sandpi client does not stop an active coding
  agent. Inspect the current files and Git state before mutating them because a
  human or another Session may have changed the shared Workspace.

## Environment Preview and agent browser automation

- Preview is the human-facing surface for HTTP services listening on
  `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` inside the remote Environment Sandbox. It does not
  accept HTTPS, IPv6 loopback, remote hosts or credentials in the URL.
- Preview is not a general browser and is not shared with the coding agent. Its
  tabs, cookies and login state live in the human's client browser on an
  isolated per-Environment/port origin. They are not a Playwright profile and
  are not included in Workspace backups.
- The agent can independently use `playwright-cli` inside the Sandbox. Read the
  locally installed `playwright-cli` skill for commands matching the installed
  version. Those pages, snapshots, cookies and logins are agent-tool state and
  are not visible in Preview; never assume a human login is available to the
  agent or vice versa.
- Preview URLs and live frames have no continuity guarantee across client
  unmount, Sandbox pause, resume, or process recovery. Reopen Preview from the
  Environment and re-check the service after recovery.

## Sandbox pause and resume

- Sandpi sets both the Sandbox0 soft TTL and hard TTL to zero for Environment
  Sandboxes. Sandpi's configurable idle-pause policy is separate from resource
  expiry and owns intentional pauses.
- Sandpi does not idle-pause an Environment while a product Session is starting
  or running, or a native Turn is active or pending. Terminal input, new Preview
  HTTP requests, and client WebSocket messages keep an already-running
  Environment active; passive open connections do not.
- A supported Workspace, Preview, Terminal, or coding-agent access can trigger
  Sandbox0 auto-resume. A wake-up may take time; wait for the native transition
  instead of creating replacement resources or calling an independent resume
  path.
- A user can explicitly pause or restart the shared Sandbox from Environment
  Settings for manual fault recovery. Restart performs one committed pause and
  resume under Sandpi's lifecycle lock. Agents should not invoke this recovery
  control as a substitute for native auto-resume unless the user requests it.
- The Workspace Volume and native Session history are durable. Process memory,
  sockets, Preview frames, live agent Playwright pages, terminal process state,
  and an in-flight model Turn are not durable runtime checkpoints. Re-read
  persisted state before continuing after recovery and avoid repeating
  external side effects. Sandpi makes no shared browser-profile durability
  contract; files an agent tool writes under the Workspace follow ordinary
  Workspace backup behavior.
- A Sandbox-caused interruption may receive one visible, bounded Sandpi recovery
  Turn. Sandpi never silently replays the original user request.
- Quota policy can pause or reject runtime access. External deletion of the
  Sandbox resource is reported as missing instead of silently provisioning a
  replacement with potentially different security settings.

## Current product surfaces

- Native Codex account connection, model and reasoning discovery, persistent
  Sessions and Turns, branching, tools, Skills, MCP, approvals, and supported
  slash-command surfaces.
- Workspace file tree and editor, Git changes, Terminal, loopback Preview,
  agent-local Playwright CLI, and current runtime metrics.
- Per-Environment memory, idle pause, manual Sandbox pause/restart recovery,
  network policy, Sandbox0-backed egress credential injection, Workspace
  backups and restore.
- Durable one-time and recurring coding-agent Schedules with run history and
  overlap protection.
- Sandpi owns users, Environment attribution, native Session references, and
  optional product entitlements. Sandbox0 owns Sandbox lifecycle, Volumes,
  network enforcement, credential injection, and usage truth.

Codex and the Web client are the currently implemented harness and client.
Sandpi is pre-1.0, so discover exact native capabilities from the running
harness instead of assuming every newer feature exists in an older deployment.
